elements.name: fastener grip, -14 (.875 in)
elements.note: 0.875 +/-0.010 in. This is the fastener actually ballooned in DETAIL B. RE-CITED 2026-08-06 (handoff traced_labels_and_ratio): the band now comes off the NAS6403 standard, not the parts list.

source_ref.note: Both the .875 nominal and the ±.010 band are printed on sheet 3: the value in the 'Grip ±.010' column, the band in that column's own header. Sheet 2 CODE block decodes the part number -- 'Dash number indicates grip in .0625 increments' (14 x .0625 = .875), 'U' after the basic number = unplated, 'D' after the dash number = drilled shank -- and sheet 2 note (a) defines what grip means: 'from the underside of head to the end of the full cylindrical portion of the shank'. WAS `kind: parts_list` / `confidence: traced` citing 217755 balloon 35, whose own note admitted 'the grip +/-.010 is untraced (NAS6403 spec absent)' -- a parts list gives the nomenclature nominal and never a band, so that label was wrong even though the value was right. Which bolt sits in this joint is still the parts list's evidence: NAS6403U14D, find 35 qty 3, ballooned in 217755 sheet 4 DETAIL B. Scan, no text layer -- read by vision from a crop, command in docs/sessions/lessons/LESSONS_20260806_traced_labels_and_ratio.md. MERGE NOTE 2026-08-06 (review/traced_labels_and_ratio): the sibling handoff citation_export_provenance had added a source_ref.export block here, naming the 2026-JUL-23 POST export of 217755 by sha256. That block was DROPPED, not lost, when the two branches merged -- it described the parts-list citation this element no longer makes, and `kind: "spec"` is exempt from the export requirement because data/inbox/specs/ is append-only, so the filename already identifies the bytes (test_every_drawing_citation_says_which_export_it_was_read_from). The 217755 evidence for WHICH bolt this is stays in prose above; if it ever needs a machine-readable export again, that sha256 is on the sibling handoff's commit and in the same block still live on fastener_grip_13.
